name: E
title: Improver wants to relax the human-distance envelope
description: The improver found that a smaller human buffer clears lift jams. It touches the safety envelope, so it needs voice approval plus a dashboard second factor.

incident.observed_behavior: Brain v3 candidate raises zone M held-out score from 0.31 to 0.58, but only if envelope.min_human_distance_m drops from 1.0 m to 0.8 m in the lift lobby.
incident.expected_behavior: Improvements stay inside the human-owned policy envelope.
incident.failure_summary: Gate passed a change that requires new authority: it relaxes a human-safety envelope limit.

root_cause_hypothesis.text: Lift jams come from robots queuing in the lobby; a 0.8 m buffer lets them queue beside the doorway instead of in the lane.

evidence_refs.summary: Gate run gate:v3 held-out score 0.58 vs 0.31 (synthetic).

escalation.reason: The policy envelope is human-owned; the improver cannot change it.

incident.plain_summary: The improver found a change that cuts lift jams a lot, but only by letting robots get closer to people.

proposal.summary: Lower the minimum human distance in the zone M lift lobby from 1.0 m to 0.8 m.
proposal.justification: Held-out score rises from 0.31 to 0.58 on locked seeds; lift jams fall from 7 to 2 per shift (ESTIMATE).
constraints: Harness re-checks against site safety rules before promotion.
proposal.plain_summary: Lower the minimum distance to people in the lift lobby from 1 metre to 0.8 metres.

facts.text: Gate run v3 scored 0.58 on held-out seeds versus 0.31 for brain v1, with the model held fixed. Without the envelope change the best candidate scored 0.39.
In replay, 0.8 metre separations occurred 14 times per shift, always with robots stationary or below 0.3 metres per second.
